sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Cloud-native interview questions cover the cloud-vendor-agnostic patterns every modern backend interview probes — the 12-factor methodology, cloud design patterns (circuit breaker, bulkhead, retry-with-backoff, ambassador, sidecar), deployment strategies (rolling, blue/green, canary, progressive delivery), disaster recovery (RPO/RTO), multi-region active/active vs active/passive trade-offs, cost optimization (FinOps), and the orchestrator-choice question (Kubernetes vs ECS vs Cloud Run vs Lambda). Pair this with the AWS, GCP, Azure or Kubernetes pages for the platform-specific surface.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Cloud-native ≠ cloud — it's the **patterns** that work in *any* cloud.

- **12-factor app** — config in env, stateless processes, log to stdout, etc.
- **Patterns** — sidecar, ambassador, circuit breaker, bulkhead.
- **Deployment** — rolling, blue/green, canary, progressive delivery.
- **DR** — RPO (data loss) + RTO (downtime); design backwards from those numbers.
- **FinOps** — cost is a non-functional requirement.

sections.body:

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Active/active** vs **active/passive** — latency vs cost vs complexity.
- **Stateless ≠ no state** — externalise state to managed stores.
- **Multi-region** — DNS-based failover or anycast; both cost.
- **Cost optimisation** — reservations + autoscaling + savings plans.
- **Vendor lock-in** is partly a myth — use managed services, abstract carefully.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd build to 12-factor, run stateless services with externalised state, use canary deploys with auto-rollback, plan DR around explicit RPO/RTO, and bake cost dashboards into the SRE rituals."*
